concepts.why: Biblical-theological and secular readers: the name is 'The arm of the LORD' and Isa 50:2 says 'My hand too short', not arm (the other seven say arm). Drop it, leaving seven; the idiom is already shown in 'Is the LORD's arm too short' (Num 11:23; Isa 59:1).

Secular scholar and every close reader: the name says 'He redeemed His people', but Luke 2:38 ('waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem') and Luke 24:21 ('we were hoping He was the One who would redeem Israel') are people waiting or hoping, not a statement that He redeemed. Drop both (six remain). Luke 2:38 could move to 61 'I wait for Your salvation', which has seven.

concepts.name: Save Yourself!
concepts.why: Pentecostal, Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran and Reformed readers: as a bare heading 'He saved others, but He cannot save Himself' reads as the site stating that He cannot, when it is the mockers' claim. 'Save Yourself!' (Matt 27:40; Luke 23:37; the 'save Himself' of Matt 27:42, Mark 15:31, Luke 23:35, and 'Save Yourself and us' of Luke 23:39) is plainly a taunt, is in six of the seven passages, and says nothing about whether it could be done. Matt 27:43 says 'deliver' not 'save Yourself', so it may stay if the heading is kept loose; dropping it leaves six.

concepts.name: Faith and works
concepts.why: Lutheran, Reformed, Wesleyan, Catholic, Orthodox: the two sides of the faith-and-works texts now sit under headings of different force. 46 is a full doctrinal sentence (Rom 3:28); 45 is an exhortation (Phil 2:12), so one side gets a verdict and the other a command, and James 2:24, the parallel verdict, is not the name. James 2:24's own words cannot be the name because Phil 2:12-13, Eph 2:10, Gal 5:6 and 1 Tim 4:16 do not say 'justified by deeds'. A plain label (as 'Baptism' is) is neutral to both. Passages stay as they are.

Secular scholar and Jewish readers of the Hebrew Bible, Catholic: the name says 'justified by faith apart from works of the law'. Gen 15:6 and Hab 2:4 say neither 'justified' nor 'apart from works of the law'; placing them under that sentence presents Paul's reading of them (Rom 4, Gal 3) as what they say, which is the Old Testament pointing to the New. Hab 2:4 is also read in Jewish tradition as faithfulness. Drop both; Rom 4:5 quotes Gen 15:6 in its own words. Five remain.

note_fixes: Acts 16:33-34 (replace Acts 16:33): 'he and all his household were baptized' and 'he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God'
concepts.why: Baptist and Reformed readers: Acts 16:33 alone gives the household-baptism text to one side with the believing half of the same story cut off, while the other side gets Mark 16:16, Acts 2:38, 22:16 and 1 Pet 3:21 whole. Verse 34 (BSB: 'So he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God') belongs with it so each tradition finds its words. Cite as Acts 16:33-34 with a note quoting both halves.

secondary_or_links: Same sub-theme named twice: 19 'My rock, my fortress, and my deliverer' and 20 'God my Savior; the God of my salvation'. Both are the psalmist's address to God as his deliverer or salvation; 19 already holds Ps 62:2, 89:26, 95:1 and 18:2, which say 'salvation', and the drafter's figures-versus-title line is not one the texts draw. Merge them (the combined passages would need trimming to eight), or at least tell the owner this is the one pair.

Links: the ten-link limit is lifted, and the theme's own passages run into three themes it does not link: Kingdom (secondary 'Salvation -> Kingdom'; Matt 7:13-14, John 3:3-5), The Law (concepts 46 and 53: works of the law, Gal 3:13, Gal 5:4) and Church (concepts 47 and 59). Add them if they are themes on the site.

Secondary 'Salvation -> Healing' with Isa 53:5: no change, since the verse says 'we are healed' in so many words; noted only because readers part on whether bodily healing is part of the atonement, and the link states nothing about that.

Order of the contested pairs now reads: grace (43), believe (44), faith and works (45), justified by faith (46), baptism (47), repentance (48), wants everyone (49), chose us (50), no one can snatch (51), perseveres (52), fallen away (53), know (54). Each pair runs a different way and no side has the last word; no change.
Acts 28:28 in concept 59 sits beside Luke 2:32 ('glory to Your people Israel') and Rom 9:4 in 58, which keeps Israel and the Gentiles both in view; no change.

missing.sub_theme: He will repay each man according to his deeds
missing.why: Plainly and widely developed across both Testaments, and the other half of the faith-and-works texts. Without it the works side of the salvation debate is carried by James 2 and Phil 2 alone, against grace (43), believe (44) and justified by faith (46); Catholic, Orthodox, Wesleyan and Pentecostal readers would say the weighting favours one side. Placing it near 45 keeps the texts side by side. Name is Ps 62:12 / Rom 2:6, in the Berean's words; it says nothing about how it sits with grace.
